ideas.description: Diagnostic that sharpens I013 for the current tip; it makes no recipe change. Run the E010 recipe exactly as committed (Muon, Lookahead/EMA, 24→28→32 px, 9 epochs, last group 512) offline on held-out seeds 3-12 through the same harness code path. Record per-seed accuracy, the 10-seed mean, the std and the offset from the seeds 0-2 mean (0.7548). In the same pass, record per-epoch CUDA-event times to settle H3.3.1. Do not edit submissions/arena/.
ideas.expected: Time is unchanged at about 6.6 s. The 10-seed mean is within 0.3 pp of 0.7548 and per-seed std is 0.15-0.35 pp. If the held-out mean is under 0.751, the tip is fragile for the 40-seed judgment. In that case every later trim needs at least 0.4 pp of margin, and the next experiment must buy accuracy back. Epoch 1 is under 0.3 s slower than the later epochs, which would refute H3.3.1.

ideas.description: Exploit, as a near-free accuracy lever (W1 and W3 crux). On the E010 recipe, change only the label smoothing from 0.3 to 0.2 (the airbench96_faster value) in the training loss. Epochs, resizing, Muon/SGD settings and Lookahead/EMA stay the same, and so do the compiled shapes. Since the loss changes only by a constant, no extra warm-up is needed beyond the usual error_on_recompile check.
ideas.expected: Time is unchanged (±1%, about 6.64 s). Accuracy moves between -0.3 and +0.4 pp. A gain of 0.3 pp or more supports H1.3.1 and buys about 0.5 epoch for the next trim. A loss would show that strong LS is still needed for a 100-way head in a short run, and the next test should try LS 0.35.

ideas.description: Exploit. On the E010 recipe, change only the Muon learning rate for the conv filters from 0.24 to 0.36 (×1.5). The SGD groups (BN, whitening bias, head), momentum 0.6, batch size 2000, schedule shape, epochs and Lookahead/EMA stay the same. The 0.24 value comes from CIFAR-10 airbench94_muon, and E006's surprise gain (+0.66 pp, outside every member's range) suggests the CIFAR-100 optimum has not been explored.
ideas.expected: Time is unchanged (±1%). Accuracy moves between -0.4 and +0.4 pp. A gain of 0.3 pp or more supports H1.5.1, and the run after it should try ×2. A loss of 0.2 pp or more points the next test at ×0.67.

ideas.description: Exploit, as the second point of the coarse grid. On the E010 recipe, halve only the weight decay for all parameter groups (Muon conv filters and SGD groups), keeping the same decoupled or coupled form the code uses now. Everything else stays identical. Short runs with EMA may need less regularization than the 0.012 CIFAR-10 value.
ideas.expected: Time is unchanged (±1%). Accuracy moves between -0.4 and +0.3 pp. A gain of 0.3 pp or more supports H1.5.1. A loss of more than 0.2 pp shows that wd is part of what makes the solution sharp, so the next test should try wd ×1.5.

ideas.description: Exploit on cost per step. Muon added 0.35 s (+3.8%) in E006. On the E010 recipe, cut the Newton-Schulz iterations in the Muon update from 5 to 3, keeping the same quintic coefficients and bf16. Everything else stays the same. Re-warm-up the compiled optimizer step in build, with error_on_recompile.
ideas.expected: Time falls 1.5-3% (0.1-0.2 s, to about 6.45-6.55 s). Accuracy changes between -0.25 and +0.05 pp. The idea pays off if the loss is under 0.1 pp, which is a better rate than the epoch dial (about 1.9 s/pp). A loss above 0.2 pp means orthogonalization quality matters for CIFAR-100, and NS should stay at 5 steps.

ideas.description: Explore, settling the W2/W4 crux about launch versus compute. Run torch._dynamo.explain and a short torch.profiler trace offline on the E010 train step on synthetic data: GPU augmentation, forward/backward, Muon+SGD step, Lookahead/EMA update and LR schedule. If there are graph breaks or host syncs (for example .item(), Python-scalar LR, or tensor-to-bool checks), remove them: keep LR as a GPU tensor, fold augmentation into the compiled region, and keep the math identical. Commit only the break-free version and record the measured GPU idle fraction in the notebook.
ideas.expected: Accuracy is bit-identical per seed. If explain finds at least one break or sync, time falls 2-5% (about 0.15-0.3 s). If it finds none, change the code anyway only if the profile shows GPU idle above 5%; otherwise record H2.2.3 as refuted and lower I014's priority (CUDA graphs would then have little to gain).

ideas.description: Explore, aimed at the E005 counterexample (endpoint averaging was worth about 1 pp, far more than forecast). On the E010 recipe, replace the airbench96_faster Lookahead, which resets the fast weights to the slow weights every 5 steps, with a plain EMA of weights and BN buffers. The EMA updates every 5 steps with the same alpha ramp, never writes back into the fast weights, and is copied into the model only at the end of train. Create and reset all EMA state in prepare.
ideas.expected: Time is unchanged within 1%. Accuracy lands within ±0.3 pp of 0.7548. A drop of more than 0.3 pp means the Lookahead pull-back trajectory, not endpoint averaging, drives the gain (refuting H1.3.5). A gain would suggest that longer averaging horizons are worth tuning next.

drop.reason: Rewritten as a new idea that runs the held-out-seed diagnostic on the current tip, E010 (I013 still pointed at E007 or E008, which are no longer the tip). The margin crux that all four members raised now concerns E010's 0.18 pp margin.

structured_output.summary: The tip is E010 at 6.64 s and 0.7548, which leaves only 0.18 pp of margin, so this queue puts accuracy first before any more trimming. Three exploit ideas add accuracy at no time cost and test the members' shared crux about a near-free lever. They are LS 0.3→0.2 (H1.3.1), Muon lr ×1.5 and wd ×0.5 (both H1.5.1, since E006's surprise suggests the CIFAR-10 hyperparameters are off for CIFAR-100). I013 is rewritten so the held-out-seed diagnostic runs on E010, which settles how much margin the 40-seed judgment needs. On cost per step, there is one exploit idea, Newton-Schulz 5→3 iterations to recover part of Muon's 0.35 s overhead (H1.2). There is also one explore idea, a graph-break and profile check (H2.2.3) that settles the launch-bound versus compute-bound dispute and decides whether I014 (CUDA graphs, kept in the queue) is worth running. One explore idea, plain EMA versus Lookahead (H1.3.5), probes the mechanism behind the E005 counterexample. I011 is still running and I015 stays vetoed. With I014, the queue now holds 8 ideas.
